compiled_state.title: As a sprint orchestrator, Phase E creates a story branch per dispatched story and Phase F merges it into the session branch with a DSO-Story trailer
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Phase E creates story/<id> branch off the session base for each story dispatched. Phase F merges story/<id> into the session branch using `git merge --no-ff --message=<msg-with-DSO-Story-trailer>` so the trailer is present in the merge commit message at creation time and readable by `git interpret-trailers --parse`.
**Why**: Walking-skeleton story-branch infrastructure. Without this story, no per-story isolation exists.

**Scope**:
- IN: Phase E story-branch creation in sprint orchestration (one branch per dispatched story)
- IN: Phase F merge with explicit --message= containing trailer block (DSO-Story line constructed from the active task's parent chain)
- IN: Verification helper that asserts session branch contains only merge commits between story merges
- OUT: CI workflow on push to story/* — owned by S8
- OUT: DefenseStore SHA-range protocol — owned by S10

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, post-Phase-E, git branch --list story/* shows exactly one branch per dispatched story plus optionally the orphan branch
  ← Satisfies: "SC2: Story-isolated branches with merge gating"
- When this story is complete, every session-branch merge commit produced by Phase F carries a DSO-Story trailer readable by `git interpret-trailers --parse`
  ← Satisfies: "SC2"
- When this story is complete, no non-merge commit appears on the session branch between story merges (verifiable by post-sprint script)
  ← Satisfies: "SC2"
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations

- [Reliability] Phase F merge ordering vs S10 hash-of-record SHA range: define whether story branches are static (all rooted at Phase E base) or dynamic (rebased onto each merged predecessor). The two semantics produce different attestation validity windows and different diff scopes. Document the chosen semantics and ensure S8 diff-scope and S10 SHA-range membership both align with that choice.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
